items.note: College proposal 'Indexering parkeertarieven 2024' (collegedatum 12-09-2023, decision 'Conform'), 8 pages read. Street tariffs must be >= nearby Q-Park garage tariffs under the 2003 samenwerkingsovereenkomst; footnote exempts Vrijthof for lack of nearby street spaces; policy text steers long-stay visitors to garages so street spaces stay free for short-stay visitors and permit holders (residents, businesses). It is a college paper, not a council paper (the draft says 'council papers'), minor.

Same college paper: 15 percent from 1 Jan 2024 to EUR 3.50 (was 3.00) Binnenstad, EUR 1.80 (was 1.50) overig gebied, day ticket EUR 7.80 (was 6.80). Reasons confirmed: Q-Park agreement, national tariffs +30 percent vs +15 percent in Maastricht, 2022 realised income and enforcement income about EUR 1 million below budget. College decision 'Conform'; the 2025 college paper (item 2) lists the same 2024 tariffs as the base, so they were in force.

College paper 19 Nov 2024 (decision 'Conform'; sets the Tarieventabel after the 2025 budget was adopted): street tariffs +3.3 percent, 3.50->3.60, 1.80->1.90, day 7.80->8.10; fine EUR 78.80 from 1 Jan 2025; Q-Park tariffs indexed by September CPI 3.5 percent. All as written.

College paper 14 Dec 2021 (decision 'Conform'): municipality sets Q-Park tariffs under the 2003 agreement; annual CPI indexation since 2015; equal tariffs per ring (ring 0 Vrijthof, 1 core shopping area, 2 centre, 3 Park & Walk); CPI 2.7 percent; steps ring 0 15->14 min, ring 2 26->24 min, ring 3 40->39 min; evaluation/recalculation postponed because Covid distorted traffic patterns. Matches.

Raadsstuk (college paper) 'Belastingverordeningen en tarieven Maastricht 2026': decision block dated 16 Sep 2025 'Conform' (summary text says the college meeting was 9 Sep 2025, so there is a small date inconsistency inside the paper); to the council meeting of 4 Nov 2025. 2.1 percent general index; Q-Park garages indexed by September CPI; section 1.18 says street tariffs are corrected upward if the September CPI exceeds the general index. Worded as a proposal, which is correct. The council vote itself was not found.

Live page (no date; read 21 Oct 2026) confirms EUR 3.70 per hour high tariff (mainly A-zone, i.e. city centre), EUR 1.90 low tariff (mainly B-zone) and EUR 8.30 day ticket except at places with a parking-duration limit. The page does NOT say the progressive tariff rises 'after the 1st, 2nd or 4th hour'; it only says that at certain locations an increasing hourly tariff applies and the maximum parking time lapses, with an example of two hours at EUR 3.70 and a higher price from the third hour. That detail is unsupported.
items.corrected_text: Page read on 21 October 2026: street parking costs EUR 3.70 per hour in the high-tariff zone (mainly the A-zone in the city centre), EUR 1.90 per hour in the low-tariff zone (mainly outside the singels) and EUR 8.30 for a day ticket, except at locations with a parking-duration limit. At some locations a progressive tariff applies, where the hourly rate rises the longer you park and the maximum parking time is dropped (the page's example: EUR 3.70 per hour for the first two hours, more from the third hour).

items.note: Live page read 21 Oct 2026: Mon, Tue, Wed, Fri, Sat 08.00-18.00; Thu 08.00-21.00; Sun 12.00-18.00; paid parking applies on days shops are open; on holidays with closed shops street parking is free but Q-Park locations still charge. Matches.

I viewed the flyer image itself (Flyer NED parkeertarieven Maastricht 2026, linked on the garages page; the file path is dated 2026-01). Text was clearly legible. Legend: F Vrijthof EUR 1.50 = 16 min / EUR 35 per day; E (Bassin, Mosae Forum, OLV-parking) 25 min / EUR 28.50; D (Frontenpark, Sphinx, De Griend, P+R Station, De Colonel, Plein 1992) 32 min / EUR 18; C (Stadspark, Bonnefanten) 50 min / EUR 14; footnote: P Bonnefanten max EUR 21.00 on weekdays and EUR 14 at weekends; B Fort Willem (P+W) EUR 1.90 = 60 min / EUR 8.30; A P+R Maastricht Noord free parking and EUR 2.55 p.p. by bus. Every number in the draft matches. The page text itself only carries the flyer as an image, so this rests on my reading of the image.

Live page read 21 Oct 2026: free parking, 516 spaces, Hoekerweg; EUR 1.28 per trip with OVpay; return ticket EUR 2.55 per person (until 31 Dec 2026); group return for 3-5 people EUR 6.40; monthly pass EUR 32.05. Matches.

News item dated 12 Oct 2026 is an announcement of a future change: 'Na 31 december 2026 is er geen kaartautomaat meer' and loose tickets can be bought only until 31 Dec 2026. The draft states it as done ('is removed'). The page does not state the date 1 January 2027 itself (the P+R page says 'vanaf 1 januari').
items.corrected_text: On 12 October 2026 Maastricht Bereikbaar announced that after 31 December 2026 there will no longer be a ticket machine at P+R Maastricht Noord. Loose tickets, multi-day tickets and group returns can be bought there only until 31 December 2026; afterwards travellers check in and out with OVpay (a card or ov-pas) and pay the P+R rate of EUR 1.28 per trip.

items.note: Gemeente page 'Tarieven parkeerproducten' (live, 2026) confirms: Binnenstad residents and businesses EUR 30.08 per month; Overig gebied EUR 5.03 (1st) and EUR 7.56 (2nd); application fee EUR 23.15; student EUR 6.96; temporary permit EUR 20.86 (Binnenstad) / EUR 10.43 (Overig gebied). Corrections: EUR 57.56 is the 'Woon-werkverkeer vergunning Overig Gebied' (commuter permit for the Overig gebied), not a general commuter permit; the explanation 'inside the singels' is not on this tariff page (it is on the residents' permit page, item 11).
items.corrected_text: Page read on 21 October 2026: 2026 permit tariffs for residents and businesses are EUR 30.08 per month in the Binnenstad and EUR 5.03 per month for a first and EUR 7.56 for a second permit in the Overig gebied. A commuter permit (woon-werkverkeer, Overig gebied) costs EUR 57.56 per month and a student permit EUR 6.96. A one-day temporary permit costs EUR 20.86 (Binnenstad) or EUR 10.43 (Overig gebied). The application fee is EUR 23.15.

items.note: Live page read 21 Oct 2026: from 1 Jan 2022 Binnenstad residents (inside the singels) can apply for at most one permit and only if they have no private parking; in the Overig gebied no second permit if private parking is available, existing permits unchanged; no permits can be requested for the Ceramique district; payment per year or per quarter. Matches.

News item dated 7 Jan 2026 and the Bereikbaar parking page: pilot since 5 Jan 2026, Wycker Brugstraat (between Sint Servaasbrug and Lage Barakken) closed to cars and motors Mon-Fri 18.00-07.00 and Sat 18.00 to Mon 07.00; new loading rules in Wyck; Plein 1992, De Colonel, De Griend or P+R Noord with bus 30; one year of evaluation, after which the city decides whether the rules stay. Matches.

Gemeente page (undated, live): from 1 Jan 2025 vans and lorries on petrol, diesel or LPG with emission class below 5 may not enter the Binnenstad; passenger cars are not covered; transition scheme to 2030; traffic decision and exemption policy published 25 April 2024. Matches (page is undated; the 2025 start is the event date).

Capacities confirmed on the Q-Park garage pages (read 21 Oct 2026): Mosae Forum 1089, Frontenpark 1308, Plein 1992 449, Vrijthof 447, Bassin 397, OL Vrouweparking 354, De Griend 346, P+R Station 340, Bonnefanten 297, De Colonel 289, Entre Deux 199, Stadspark I/II/III 234/84/71, P+R Meerssenerweg 66. The Q-Park pages do not mention the 2003 agreement, and Entre Deux and P+R Meerssenerweg appear in none of the council tariff tables or the flyer, so 'under the 2003 agreement' cannot be stated for the whole list.
items.corrected_text: Page read on 21 October 2026 (Q-Park garage pages list capacities): Mosae Forum 1,089 spaces, Frontenpark 1,308, Plein 1992 449, Vrijthof 447, Bassin 397, OL Vrouweparking 354, De Griend 346, P+R Station 340, Bonnefanten 297, De Colonel 289, Entre Deux 199, Stadspark I/II/III 234/84/71 and P+R Meerssenerweg 66. The city's council papers (items 3 and 4) show Q-Park tariffs for the ring garages being set under the 2003 agreement; the Q-Park pages themselves do not say which of these sites fall under it.

items.note: Gemeente page (live, read 21 Oct 2026): about 500 public charging posts with 2 charge points each (1,000), expected to double to 2,000 charge points in 2030 together with Vattenfall InCharge; pilot with cable-gutter tiles from 1 Aug 2025 with up to 50 participants. Matches.

Page (undated, live) describes 'Topdagen Plus' with traffic regulator (verkeersregisseur), static and dynamic signs, PRIS signs showing free garage spaces, possible closure of routes from Statensingel, Frontensingel and Bassinbrug, extra Q-Park parking hosts. But overflow lots are not deployed: it lists only a 'possible extension' at existing sites such as P+R Noord and says extra overflow lots 'blijft achter de hand' because Frontenpark (opened June 2024) added more than 900 spaces versus December 2023. Allerheiligen, Allerzielen, Hemelvaart, André Rieu, Magisch Maastricht and neighbouring countries' holidays are named.
items.corrected_text: Page read on 21 October 2026: on especially busy days (holidays such as Allerheiligen and Allerzielen, events such as Magisch Maastricht and André Rieu, and holidays in neighbouring countries) the city, Maastricht Bereikbaar and Q-Park run 'Topdagen Plus' measures: a municipal traffic coordinator, extra traffic regulators, static and dynamic signs, signs showing free garage spaces (PRIS), possible closure of routes from Statensingel, Frontensingel and Bassinbrug, extra Q-Park parking hosts and extra enforcement. Extra overflow car parks (for example next to P+R Noord) are kept in reserve rather than used by default, because the June 2024 opening of P Frontenpark added more than 900 spaces.

items.note: Live page read 21 Oct 2026: for arrivals from Lanaken/Smeermaas advice is Brusselseweg and Belvedere route, Fort Willem EUR 8.30 per day and Frontenpark EUR 18 with ticket; pre-booked via Q-Park from EUR 12, dynamic, never above EUR 17.50; garages in the centre often fill up quickly, especially at weekends. The advice comes from Maastricht Bereikbaar (the regional accessibility programme), not 'the city', and the Frontenpark walk-up price (EUR 18) is omitted from the draft.
items.corrected_text: Page read on 21 October 2026: Maastricht Bereikbaar advises drivers from Belgium (Lanaken/Smeermaas) to take the Brusselseweg and enter Maastricht via the Belvedere route, and to park cheaply at Fort Willem (fixed EUR 8.30 per day) or Frontenpark (EUR 18 with a ticket; pre-booked via Q-Park from EUR 12, a dynamic price never above EUR 17.50). It also says garages near the centre often fill up quickly, especially at weekends.

corrected_summary: Maastricht prices parking by distance from the centre in a ring structure. Q-Park garage tariffs are set by the municipality under a 2003 public-private agreement and indexed each year by the September consumer price index, and street tariffs must be at or above the tariffs of nearby garages. The college raised street tariffs by 15 percent for 2024 and by 3.3 percent for 2025. A college proposal for 2026, sent to the council for 4 November 2025 (the council vote was not found), applies a 2.1 percent general index. In October 2026 the Maastricht Bereikbaar page showed street parking at EUR 3.70 per hour in the high-tariff zone, EUR 1.90 elsewhere and EUR 8.30 for a day ticket. A 2026 flyer, which I read as an image, gives garage tariffs from EUR 1.50 per 16 minutes with a EUR 35 day maximum at Vrijthof down to EUR 14 per day at Stadspark, with Fort Willem (Park & Walk) at EUR 8.30 per day. Q-Park capacity figures from its garage pages include Mosae Forum 1,089, Frontenpark 1,308, Plein 1992 449, Vrijthof 447, Bassin 397 and Entre Deux 199 spaces. Policy steers long-stay visitors to garages, Park & Walk sites and P+R Noord (free, 516 spaces; the ticket machine there is announced to go after 31 December 2026). Resident permits cost EUR 30.08 per month in the Binnenstad, where residents can hold one permit and only without private parking. A zero-emission zone for delivery vehicles has applied since 1 January 2025, and a one-year autoluw Wyck pilot began on 5 January 2026. On busy days Maastricht Bereikbaar, the city and Q-Park run extra traffic management and advise Belgian visitors on routes and cheap car parks. No usage statistics or council debates on a new parking policy were found.
